title: Battery Storage Inspection Checklist Form
subtitle: An original battery storage workflow that guides a bounded inspection from readiness through findings and release, with explicit qualified-review, stop-work, escalation, and accountable handoff controls.
description: A workflow-complete battery storage inspection checklist form for the stationary battery energy storage system that captures exact identity, domain observations, supporting evidence, decisions, exceptions, responsible owners, and closeout without replacing professional judgment or the organization's controlling procedures.
use_case: Use when an assigned inspector must confirm safe observation boundaries, document domain-specific conditions, route deficiencies, and record a qualified acceptance, restriction, or follow-up decision. The energy storage operations lead owns routing, and closure requires documented evidence, disposition of restrictions, and acceptance by the designated reviewer.

sections.title: Battery storage inspection identity and authority
sections.guidance: Define the asset, inspection scope, qualified reviewer, and conditions before observations begin.

sections.title: Battery storage readiness and safe observation boundary
sections.guidance: Confirm identity, operating context, access, and limits before checking condition.

blocks.label: Stop-work boundary
blocks.guidance: Do not open, enter, touch, reset, or approach a battery system showing heat, smoke, flame, hissing, odor, swelling, leaking, water intrusion, impact damage, or an isolation alarm. Keep people clear and activate the site emergency plan. Stored or stranded energy may remain after shutdown; only designated qualified personnel may assess isolation, recovery, and return to service.

sections.title: Battery storage inspection points and finding evidence
sections.guidance: Check each point only when observed; use the findings table for condition, evidence, and disposition.

blocks.label: Domain inspection checklist
items: System, chemistry, rack, module, PCS, inverter, BMS, and enclosure identities agree
Access control, warning labels, clearances, housekeeping, and responder information are intact
Enclosure, doors, seals, vents, cable entries, and impact protection show no damage
No swelling, deformation, leak, residue, hissing, unusual odor, smoke, or heat is observed
HVAC, ventilation, detection, suppression, and environmental status are normal or escalated
BMS, PCS, inverter, communications, alarms, and event history are captured remotely where possible
SOC, SOH, voltage, current, temperature spread, and isolation indicators are logged
Grounding, bonding, disconnect, protective, and emergency-stop references are documented
Water intrusion, flood, condensation, corrosion, and drainage conditions are checked
Operating mode, dispatch command, critical-load impact, and maintenance window are confirmed
Manufacturer restrictions, support case, and emergency-plan routing are current
Any abnormal condition remains restricted until qualified review and explicit release

fields.label: Inaccessible areas, sampling limits, representative conditions, trends, and supporting context

sections.title: Battery storage exceptions, stop conditions, and escalation
sections.guidance: Make every unresolved condition visible with an immediate control, owner, due point, and final disposition.

blocks.label: Stop-condition screen
items: Smoke, flame, rapid heat rise, hissing, popping, or unusual odor
Swelling, deformation, electrolyte residue, leak, or damaged cell enclosure
Thermal, gas, fire-detection, suppression, or ventilation alarm
Water intrusion, flooding, condensation, or damaged environmental seal
Impact, penetration, dropped module, damaged cable, or exposed conductor
Unknown isolation, stranded charge, backfeed, or reaccumulating stored energy
Manufacturer stop condition or emergency-plan activation threshold
Any entry or task beyond the person's training, PPE, tools, or authorization
blocks.guidance: Check any condition observed or reported; checking an item does not mean the condition is controlled.

blocks.label: Qualified-person and stop-work boundary
blocks.guidance: Do not open, enter, touch, reset, or approach a battery system showing heat, smoke, flame, hissing, odor, swelling, leaking, water intrusion, impact damage, or an isolation alarm. Keep people clear and activate the site emergency plan. Stored or stranded energy may remain after shutdown; only designated qualified personnel may assess isolation, recovery, and return to service.

blocks.label: Exception and escalation register
blocks.guidance: Link each inspection exception to supporting evidence and keep it open until disposition is recorded.

sections.title: Battery storage decision, handoff, and accountable closeout
sections.guidance: Record the decision, remaining limitations, next action, and the people accountable for acceptance.

blocks.label: Closeout completeness
items: Stationary battery energy storage system identity and location were reconciled
Observed facts, measurements, and evidence references are complete
Decision authority and applicable review requirements were confirmed
Stop conditions, restrictions, and open exceptions remain visible
Customer, operations, or site handoff was recorded
Next action, owner, due point, and record-retention route are explicit

fields.label: Limitations, assumptions, restrictions, customer message, and next-action context

blocks.label: Accountable review and handoff
blocks.guidance: Signatures acknowledge the recorded decision and handoff; they do not waive unresolved restrictions.
